examples.title: The deliberately risky token (deployed for this demo)

flags.title: Deployed 6 minutes ago
flags.plain: This contract was deployed very recently. Most scams and mistakes are caught within days; this one has not had that time, so there is no track record to lean on.

flags.title: One key controls the contract
flags.plain: A single wallet can create new tokens out of thin air (dilute every holder); freeze or block specific addresses so they cannot move their tokens; change the fee or tax taken on transfers; pause all transfers. If that key is lost, stolen or misused, holders have no protection.

flags.title: The contract can destroy itself
flags.plain: The code contains the instruction that deletes a contract. Where the chain still honours it, whoever can call that path can remove the contract and take what it holds.

flags.title: Runs outside code as its own
flags.plain: The code can execute code from another address as if it were its own. If an administrator can choose that address, they can do anything the contract can do.
